title: Seven Winners
paragraphs: Following one of the closest championship battles in Formula One history, expectations were high heading into 2012. Red Bull's Sebastian Vettel returned as the reigning double World Champion, but McLaren, Ferrari, Mercedes and Lotus all appeared capable of challenging for victories in what would become one of the most competitive seasons of the modern era.

The season began in extraordinary fashion, with the opening seven Grands Prix producing seven different winners from five different teams. Lewis Hamilton, Jenson Button, Fernando Alonso, Nico Rosberg, Sebastian Vettel, Mark Webber and Pastor Maldonado all stood on the top step before any driver had managed a second victory, highlighting just how unpredictable the competitive order had become.

As the season progressed, the championship gradually evolved into a battle between Vettel and Alonso. While Vettel's Red Bull grew stronger after the summer break, Alonso kept an inconsistent Ferrari firmly in title contention through a series of remarkable drives, ensuring the championship remained alive until the final race in Brazil.

Vettel ultimately secured his third consecutive World Championship by just three points, despite recovering from a first-lap spin in the title decider. Although remembered for its dramatic conclusion, 2012's legacy lies in its remarkable competitiveness, with eight different race winners, seven winners in the opening seven races, and one of the deepest fields Formula One has ever seen.
